title: Time to Change: A Multilevel Analysis of the Enduring Effects of the Pandemic in the Restaurant Sector
content: The COVID-19 pandemic has meant a serious risk to the economic viability of companies and the sustainability of employment in the restaurant sector, an important industry and employment provider in Mexico and Spain. This paper analyzes the causes of prolonged and intense destruction for companies and employees via multilevel analysis techniques and a qualitative, inductive methodology drawing on multiple sources. The model posits that the sectoral structure, management practices, and institutional actions during and after the pandemic are predictors of business recovery or continued losses. In the event of a demand shock, the combination of low institutional protection at the macro level, a hostile industry structure at the meso level, and a focus solely on economic sustainability as the primary business objective resulted in widespread resignation and put survival at risk, particularly for smaller companies and entrepreneurs. In an asymmetrical and fragmented marketplace, recuperating consumer demand requires skilled human capital and know-how that can be difficult to acquire when labor practices are abusive to employees, with precarious contracts and low wages. In conclusion, addressing the sector's shortcomings requires a profound change in managing key assets, such as human capital, to acquire the capacity for flexibility, adaptability, and innovation essential for change and renewal.
